narr: An anomalously moist airmass ahead of a frontal boundary sparked numerous showers and thunderstorms across Virginia. Instantaneous rain rates approached five to six inches an hour in the bigger storms. Storm total rainfall of one and a half to four inches resulted in flooding and flash flooding in areas throughout the evening of July 9th.
ev: Parts of Thomas Nelson Highway near Davis Creek Lane closed due to flooding from 6 to 12 inches of water flowing over the water.
The 1400 block of Thomas Nelson Highway closed due to 2 to 3 feet of standing water.
Southbound lanes of Thomas Nelson Highway closed between 13000 and 14000 block due to a mudslide. Snow plows used to move debris.
Milton Road at Henderson Creek closed due to high water. Creek reported to be flowing over the road, at least 12 inches in depth.
Cars stuck in high water in the 100-200 block of East Monroe and 3 East Glebe. Water at least one to two feet deep.
Approximately 1.5 to 3 feet of standing water near Braddock Road Metro Station.
